stories.title: Dwight Refis LA-Area Apartments With $62M Loan
stories.excerpt: GR Properties USA has sealed $62 million of bridge debt to refinance a newly developed multifamily project in suburban Los Angeles, Commercial Observer has learned. Dwight Investment Management, an affiliate of Dwight Capital, closed the loan for the 139-unit Lana property in Culver City, Calif. The financing was originated by Dwight’s Katie Goldenberg and will fund an interest reserve in addition to paying down both past debt and preferred equity on the development, according to Dwight. First Draw Capital negotiated the debt with a team led by Antonio Hachem and Kyle Redmond. Hachem, co-founder and principal of First Draw Capital, said in a statement that the lending process by Dwight focused “on the strength of the project while working through a complicated structure.” Located at 10375 Washington Boulevard 11 miles west of Downtown Los Angeles, the seven-story Lana property features a unit mix of 13 studios, 95 one-bedroom units and 31 two-bedroom units. The property also has 2,000 square feet of commercial space along with community amenities that include a pool, a cabana, a fitness center, a clubhouse, a rooftop recreation area, a bike repair shop, electric vehicle charging stations and coworking spaces. GR Properties USA, which is run by Bill Wei, did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com
bullets: GR Properties USA refinanced 139-unit Lana in Culver City, CA with $62M bridge debt.
Dwight Investment Management originated loan; covers interest reserve, past debt, preferred equity paydown.
Seven-story property mix: 13 studios, 95 one-bed, 31 two-bed plus 2,000 SF retail space.
stories.summary: GR Properties closed $62 million bridge financing on the Lana, a 139-unit newly developed multifamily project in Culver City, 11 miles west of Downtown Los Angeles. The seven-story property contains 13 studios, 95 one-bedroom units, and 31 two-bedroom units, plus 2,000 square feet of commercial space. Dwight Investment Management originated the loan, which funds an interest reserve and pays down prior debt and preferred equity.
stories.impact: Bridge activity on stabilized suburban LA multifamily signals strong investor appetite for recently completed Class A product; capital availability and refinance feasibility remain robust despite macro uncertainty. Culver City's position west of DTLA continues attracting development capital as demand for suburban-proximate apartments persists.

stories.title: AI Real Estate Platform Orbital Leases 11K SF at 40 West 25th Street
stories.excerpt: An artificial intelligence platform used to aid real estate attorneys is relocating its Manhattan office just a few blocks north, Commercial Observer has learned. Orbital signed an 11,185-square-foot lease for the entire sixth floor of the Kaufman Organization’s 40 West 25th Street in a move from 18 West 18th Street, which has served as a temporary office, according to tenant broker JLL. Asking rent and the length of the lease were not immediately disclosed, but the average office asking rent in Midtown South was $85.73 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to a report from CBRE. “Orbital wanted an office that could support its next phase of growth while helping the company attract and retain the right talent,” JLL’s Valentin Stobetsky, who represented the tenant alongside Evan Margolin, said in a statement. “We worked closely with the team to identify a space that met its operational needs and provided the accessibility, energy and amenities its employees value. The full floor at 40 West 25th Street delivers that ideal combination.” Grant Greenspan and Michael Kaufman represented Kaufman Investments, the division of the Kaufman Organization that officially owns the building alongside AXA Insurance. Founded in 2018, Orbital has additional offices in Los Angeles and London and supports more than 250,000 property transactions each year, according to JLL. “New York sits at the heart of both the U.S. legal and real estate industries, making it a natural headquarters for Orbital as we continue building technology purpose-built for the asset class and reshaping how real estate transactions get done,” Will Pearce, CEO and co-founder of Orbital, said in a statement. Other tenants in the 12-story building include vintage clothing retailer Hearts of Gold, which signed a 6,671-square-foot lease in 2023. bullets: AI platform Orbital leases 11,185 SF (entire 6th floor) at 40 West 25th Street, Manhattan.
Tenant relocating north from temporary 18 West 18th Street for growth and talent retention.
Midtown South office asking rent: $85.73/SF in Q2 2026; lease terms not disclosed.
stories.summary: Orbital, an AI platform serving real estate attorneys, signed an 11,185-square-foot lease for the entire sixth floor of 40 West 25th Street in Manhattan, relocating from a temporary office at 18 West 18th Street. The move supports the company's next phase of growth and talent attraction. Midtown South office asking rent averaged $85.73 per square foot in Q2 2026.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. However, tech tenant expansion in Midtown South suggests sustained office recovery and continued worker demand in Manhattan; secondary effect: sustained demand for rental housing in high-wage tech/professional submarkets near Flatiron/Midtown South.

stories.title: Waller Urges Patience, but Bond Market Keeps Rate Hike in Play
stories.excerpt: Executive Summary Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller is preaching patience before the central bank’s interest-rate decision next week. The bond market, however, is signaling that policymakers may have less room to wait as stable growth, higher energy prices and fiscal concerns keep upward pressure on Treasury yields. Investors can position for the uncertainty through short-duration income, inflation protection and selective curve trades rather than making an all-or-nothing bet on the Fed’s next decision. Inflation Data Hold the Key In a speech last week, Waller said inflation remains meaningfully above the Federal Open Market Committee’s 2% objective, but “recent data suggest we are finally seeing some signs of disinflation.” Waller said he would support maintaining the federal funds target at 3.5% to 3.75% if incoming reports confirm that improvement. If August data show the moderation was temporary, he said a rate increase could be appropriate when the FOMC meets Sept. 15-16. His comments initially cut the market-implied probability of a quarter-point increase to approximately 50% from nearly 65%. Stronger-than-expected August payroll growth subsequently shifted pricing back toward a hike, with federal funds futures assigning about a 60% probability to an increase as of Tuesday, according to CME FedWatch tool. Friday’s consumer price index report is therefore likely to carry more weight than a typical monthly release. A benign core reading could validate Waller’s wait-and-see approach. Another upside surprise, particularly in services or energy-sensitive categories, would strengthen the case for tightening. Oil is complicating the outlook. Brent crude approached $100 a barrel Tuesday as renewed Middle East hostilities threatened energy supplies. Higher fuel costs can quickly affect headline inflation and eventually filter into transportation, manufacturing, and consumer prices. bullets: Fed Governor Waller signals patience on rate hikes; bond market prices 60% probability of increase.
August payroll strength and Brent crude near $100/barrel shift inflation expectations upward.

stories.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller urged patience before the FOMC's September 15–16 meeting, noting recent disinflation signs but emphasizing inflation remains above the 2% target. Bond markets, however, now price approximately 60% odds of a rate hike after stronger-than-expected August payroll growth. Oil prices approaching $100/barrel and fiscal concerns keep upward pressure on Treasury yields; Friday's CPI reading will be pivotal.
stories.impact: Rate volatility directly affects multifamily construction financing costs, cap rates, and development underwriting assumptions. Uncertain Fed trajectory pressures floating-rate debt and refinancing feasibility for developers. Higher rates compress NOI multiples and reduce development starts; developers should stress scenarios assuming 25–50 bps of additional tightening into Q4 2026.

stories.title: Crescent Starts Work on 313-Unit Nashville Rental Community
stories.excerpt: Crescent Communities is developing NOVEL oneC1TY, a new 313-unit residential community planned for oneC1TY, the mixed-use destination at the intersection of I-440 and Charlotte Avenue in West Nashville. Upon completion in 2029, NOVEL oneC1TY will include 313 studio, one-, two-, and three-bedroom units. Amenities onsite will feature a resort-style rooftop pool deck with scenic landscaping, a bar for social gatherings with sand volleyball, a stylish resident clubhouse, a library, a fitness center built for training and recovery, a courtyard complete with fire pits and outdoor kitchen space, and an airy top-level Sky Lounge with unobstructed views of the iconic Nashville skyline. KTGY is the project designer. NOVEL oneC1TY marks the latest investment in Crescent Communities’ Nashville pipeline. Other recent updates in the market include continued leasing at NOVEL Manchester Farm and HARMON West Meade, as well as the start of construction at NOVEL Richland Creek. Legacy properties include NOVEL Edgehill, Harpeth Heights, Camden West Nashville, The Sawyer at One Bellevue Place, Heartwood at Lockwood Glen, and Cadence Cool Springs. NOVEL represents Crescent Communities’ urban Class A multifamily brand, while HARMON is its single-family build-to-rent platform. bullets: Crescent Communities begins construction on NOVEL oneC1TY: 313 units, West Nashville at I-440/Charlotte.
Completion targeted for 2029; mixed unit types (studios, 1/2/3-bed) with resort amenities.
Part of broader Crescent pipeline: leasing active at NOVEL Manchester Farm, HARMON West Meade; construction starting at NOVEL Richland Creek.
stories.summary: Crescent Communities has begun construction on NOVEL oneC1TY, a 313-unit mixed-use residential community in West Nashville at the intersection of I-440 and Charlotte Avenue, with completion expected in 2029. The project will offer studio, one-, two-, and three-bedroom units and include amenities such as a rooftop pool deck, fitness center, clubhouse, and Sky Lounge. This marks one of several active Crescent projects in Nashville's expanding market.
stories.impact: Crescent's aggressive Nashville pipeline (three concurrent developments) signals confidence in sustained rental demand and absorption in West Nashville submarkets. I-440 corridor proximity offers strong commute access to job centers; continued supply absorption will pressure rents if employment growth in the market slows, but current velocity suggests developer confidence in job migration and millennial inflow to Nashville.

stories.title: 10 Counties Hold 42% of U.S. Data Centers. Home Prices Rise Faster There.
stories.excerpt: A new report from the National Association of Realtors (NAR) has determined that only a few U.S. counties are home to the ongoing data center development boom, and that the construction of these facilities raises home values and improves local economic performance, namely household incomes. The findings of the NAR 2026 Data Center Impact Report — first reported by Commercial Observer — conclude that data centers do impact housing values and local economies, but there’s no uniform national assessment as it varies from locality to locality. “There is no single data center effect,” Lawrence Yun, chief economist of NAR, said in a statement. “Instead, the story varies significantly depending on the local market.” Using national, state and city data from 3,200 U.S. counties, NAR found that 92 percent of U.S. counties do not have a single data center in their boundaries, and that 10 counties hold nearly half (42 percent) of all data centers nationwide, with Loudoun County and Price William County in Northern Virginia alone accounting for 19 percent of U.S. data centers. Silicon Valley in Northern California and Franklin and Licking counties in central Ohio together account for 10 percent of data center development nationwide. NAR data did conclude, however, that those areas which have clusters of data centers do in fact have stronger housing markets. For instance, in counties with more than 10 data centers, the median home value came out to $431,750, while the median home value in U.S. counties without data centers is $174,500. Perhaps more interesting, counties with 10 or more data centers saw their home values increase by 95 percent between 2014 and 2024. Meanwhile, median incomes were $89,000 in the data center cluster counties (compared to the $64,000 average in communities without data centers), and employment grew by 16 percent, (compared to 2 percent growth in those counties without data centers) in that same period, according to NAR. Loudoun and Prince William counties (Northern Virginia) alone hold 19% of U.S. data centers.
Data center construction correlates with faster home-price appreciation and higher household incomes locally.
stories.summary: The National Association of Realtors' 2026 Data Center Impact Report found that 10 counties hold 42 percent of all U.S. data centers, with Loudoun and Prince William counties in Northern Virginia accounting for 19 percent alone. Ninety-two percent of U.S. counties have zero data centers. The report concludes data centers drive higher home values and household incomes, though effects vary by locality.
stories.impact: Data-center-anchored markets (Northern Virginia, Northern California, Texas, Arizona) will experience sustained job and population in-migration, driving multifamily rental demand in surrounding submarkets. Developers should prioritize land acquisition and zoning in secondary rings around data-center hubs; these spillover markets absorb workforce housing faster than broader regional trends suggest. Northern Virginia multifamily remains undersupplied relative to this structural tech-infrastructure demand.

stories.title: Development Group Inks $58M Construction Loan for Coconut Grove Condos
stories.excerpt: A development team closed on a $58 million construction loan to build The Lincoln, a luxury boutique condominium with 48 residences in Coconut Grove, Florida. The project has begun construction and is scheduled for completion by Q3 2028. Berkadia’s Scott Wadler, Bobby Dockerty, Mitch Sinberg, Matt Robbins and Brad Williamson secured the financing on behalf of the development team: LORE Development Group (a joint venture formed by Leste Group and Opportunity Fundo de Investimento Imobiliário) and Element Development. SME Capital provided the 30-month construction loan, which includes two six-month extension options. Located at 2650 Lincoln Avenue in Coconut Grove, The Lincoln features a collection of one- to four-bedroom residences, with private balconies. Building amenities at The Lincoln include a 40-foot-long heated rooftop pool, fitness center, golf simulator, co-working lounge and media area. The Lincoln was designed by Paredes Architects. Winmar Construction is the general contractor for the project, which is scheduled to be completed by Q3 2028. The post Development Group Inks $58M Construction Loan for Coconut Grove Condos appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: LORE/Element Development closed $58M construction loan for The Lincoln: 48-unit luxury condo in Coconut Grove.
SME Capital provided 30-month term with two 6-month extension options; completion Q3 2028.
Mix: 1–4 bedroom units; rooftop pool, fitness, golf simulator, co-working, media lounge.
stories.summary: A development joint venture (LORE Development Group and Element Development) closed a $58 million construction loan for The Lincoln, a 48-unit luxury boutique condominium in Coconut Grove, Florida, at 2650 Lincoln Avenue. SME Capital provided the 30-month financing with extension options. The project has begun construction with a scheduled completion date of Q3 2028 and features one- to four-bedroom residences with full amenities.
stories.impact: Coconut Grove condo financing availability remains solid despite broader credit tightening; luxury segment absorbs capital-as-equity from South Florida's high-net-worth demographic. However, 48 units is small-scale; developer appetite for boutique luxury (vs. large workforce multifamily) suggests bifurcated capital markets—institutional investors favor stabilized, higher-density products. No broader rental demand signal.

stories.title: Pebb Secures $223M Refi on Delray Beach Mixed-Use Venture
stories.excerpt: Pebb Capital secured a $223 million refinancing for Sundy Village, its seven-acre mixed-use campus in Downtown Delray Beach. Provided by J.P. Morgan and Hudson Bay Capital, the deal replaces the project’s existing construction loan while providing additional capital for tenant improvements across the 97% pre-leased development,. The financing was arranged by Walker & Dunlop’s Institutional Advisory Practice, led by Sean Reimer, Aaron Appel, Jonathan Schwartz, Keith Kurland, Adam Schwartz, and Dustin Stolly. Aaron Casden served as the J.P. Morgan banker on the transaction. Phase One delivered 100,000 square feet of Class A+ office space, 30,000 square feet of retail and dining and 268 below-grade parking spaces. The next phase includes a 79,141-square-foot standalone office building at 100 SE First Ave. for DigitalBridge, along with a 165-space parking garage at 48 SE First Ave. with approximately 3,400 square feet of ground-floor retail. Sundy Village was designed by Gensler and RLC Architects. The post Pebb Secures $223M Refi on Delray Beach Mixed-Use Venture appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Pebb Capital refinanced Sundy Village (Delray Beach mixed-use) for $223M via JP Morgan/Hudson Bay.
Phase One delivered: 100K SF office, 30K SF retail, 268 parking; 97% pre-leased.
Phase Two underway: 79K SF office (DigitalBridge tenant), 165-space parking garage, 3.4K SF retail.
stories.summary: Pebb Capital secured a $223 million refinancing for Sundy Village, a seven-acre mixed-use campus in Downtown Delray Beach, replacing the construction loan and providing additional capital for tenant improvements. Phase One is complete with 100,000 square feet of Class A+ office, 30,000 square feet of retail/dining, and 268 parking spaces across 97 percent pre-leased occupancy. Phase Two includes a 79,141-square-foot office building pre-leased to DigitalBridge and a 165-space parking garage with ground-floor retail.
stories.impact: Delray Beach mixed-use funding reflects strong South Florida office recovery and demonstrated corporate tenant demand (DigitalBridge anchor). Refinance structure (construction-to-permanent) signals lender confidence in stabilization; downstream effect: continued density and vertical mixed-use development feasibility in Downtown Delray as Class A office market re-establishes. Multifamily not directly involved, but office-retail-parking ecosystems support nearby rental housing demand.

stories.title: JV to Deliver 462K-SF Gastonia Distribution Building
stories.excerpt: The Davis Companies and joint venture Intersect Development Group are teaming up to build a Class-A distribution building at 2550 Jenkins Dairy Road in Gastonia, North Carolina. The Gastonia development will deliver a 462,000 square-foot, cross-dock distribution building to accommodate modern logistics and manufacturing users. The new facility will feature 40’ clear height, 100 dock doors, 215 trailer parking spaces, 328 auto parking spaces, and an ESFR sprinkler system. A fully circulating loop road and secured truck court give the site flexibility to support either a single-user or multi-tenant configuration. Just west of Charlotte along Interstate 85, the Gastonia facility offers strong international connectivity while supporting potential tenant operations and workforce access. The expected completion date is January 2027. Davis continues to expand its industrial platform in the Southeast, where transportation infrastructure, population growth and tenant demand support long-term investment. The post JV to Deliver 462K-SF Gastonia Distribution Building appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Davis Companies/Intersect Development deliver 462K SF cross-dock distribution facility in Gastonia, NC.
40-foot clear height, 100 dock doors, 215 trailer spaces; completion January 2027.
Site west of Charlotte on I-85 offers international connectivity and workforce access.
stories.summary: Davis Companies and Intersect Development Group are building a 462,000-square-foot Class A cross-dock distribution facility at 2550 Jenkins Dairy Road in Gastonia, North Carolina, with completion expected January 2027. The facility features 40-foot clear height, 100 dock doors, 215 trailer parking spaces, and flexible single- or multi-tenant configurations. The location west of Charlotte along I-85 provides strong regional and international logistics connectivity.
stories.impact: Gastonia distribution build signals continued industrial supply-chain relocation away from coastal congestion toward Southeast logistics hubs; driver of job creation and worker in-migration to Piedmont region. Multifamily developers should monitor Gastonia submarket for workforce housing demand; similar third- and fourth-tier industrial markets (I-85 corridor) generate rental demand for service workers, drivers, and management talent. Secondary effect: broader NC industrial growth (Charlotte, Greensboro, Raleigh) fuels multifamily absorption in gateway markets.

stories.title: Nadeem Meghji Exits Blackstone After Less Than a Year as Global Real Estate Head
stories.excerpt: Nadeem Meghji is departing from Blackstone less than a year after being named sole head of global head of real estate. Meghji’s exit from the investment leviathan follows an exodus of other executives, including Kathleen McCarthy, who until November was global co-head of real estate with Meghji, the Wall Street Journal first reported. David Levine, who co-heads real estate in the Americas for Blackstone, and Giovanni Cutaia, president of Blackstone’s real estate business, have been elevated to Meghji’s place. Blackstone did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but Blackstone President Jonathan Gray told the Wall Street Journal that, “Despite this departure, we have a business with an enormous amount of continuity and tremendous talent. … David and Gio are prime examples of that.” Meghji joined Blackstone in 2008 in the midst of the Great Recession, and the Journal reports that he is leaving his post to focus on family. In his nearly two decades at Blackstone, Meghji had a hand in expanding its data center strategy, which reached a $185 billion value as of July 2026. At the same time, the company was reporting 20 percent year-over-year growth across total revenues, fee revenues, fee-related earnings, net realization and distributable earnings. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Nadeem Meghji exits Blackstone after <1 year as global real estate head; David Levine and Giovanni Cutaia elevated.
Meghji joined 2008; expanded data center strategy to $185B value (July 2026).
Executive turnover follows departure of Kathleen McCarthy (former global co-head); organizational realignment underway.
stories.summary: Nadeem Meghji is departing Blackstone less than a year after being named sole global head of real estate. His exit follows the earlier departure of Kathleen McCarthy, the former global co-head. David Levine and Giovanni Cutaia, co-heads of real estate in the Americas, have been elevated to replace him. Meghji, who joined Blackstone in 2008, significantly expanded the firm's data center strategy to a $185 billion valuation as of July 2026.
stories.impact: Minor to multifamily development directly, but signals potential strategic shifts at the world's largest real estate investor. Blackstone's continued emphasis on data-center and infrastructure plays over traditional multifamily suggests limited appetite for large-scale residential starts at scale; implies capital competition from mega-funds will remain fierce in acquisitions and institutional-grade projects. Developers competing for Blackstone co-investment capital should emphasize data-driven, tech-enabled, mixed-use assets.

stories.title: Jay Badame Joins Bravo Group Three Years After Termination From AECOM Tishman
stories.excerpt: Jay Badame is back in action three years after being forced out as president of AECOM Tishman, Commercial Observer has learned. The development executive who had a leading role in rebuilding the World Trade Center campus has started a new position as chief operating officer at architecture, engineering and construction management firm Bravo Group, where he will manage its public- and private-sector projects, according to the company. Badame has worked on other projects like John F. Kennedy International Airport‘s new Terminals 1 and 6, as well as SL Green Realty’s One Vanderbilt prior to his termination from AECOM Tishman. During the One Vanderbilt project, he cultivated a relationship with Bravo Group President and CEO Ehab Shehata. “With the relationships that I’ve developed over the last 30 or 40 years, I’m starting to set up meetings with myself, Ehab and private-sector clients to see how Bravo can increase its market share on the architecture and engineering side,” Badame told CO. “I think there’s a void in the space for small companies. … On some of the smaller projects it’s better if we go it alone.” Bravo’s two subsidiaries are Velocity Architecture and Engineering Group and Bradford Construction. Together the companies have about 150 employees, which Badame plans to grow. The two companies are mainly involved in public sector work for clients such as the Metropolitan Transportation Authority, the New York City School Construction Authority and the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey. Badame began the new role Aug. 16, overseeing 70 employees, and joined Bravo Group’s board of advisers, which also includes former New York Gov. David Paterson, according to Bravo. “I have had the privilege of working with Jay for decades and can confidently say there is no one better suited to help Bravo usher in our next chapter of growth,” Shehata said in a statement. “He brings not only an unmatched level of expertise and experience to th
bullets: Jay Badame joins Bravo Group as COO; returning 3 years after AECOM Tishman termination.
Led WTC rebuild, JFK Terminals 1/6, and One Vanderbilt; cultivated Bravo CEO relationship.
Role: manage Bravo's public- and private-sector projects; expand market share in AEC services.
stories.summary: Jay Badame, the development executive who led the World Trade Center campus rebuild and worked on JFK International Airport terminals and SL Green's One Vanderbilt, has joined Bravo Group as chief operating officer after being forced out from AECOM Tishman three years ago. At Bravo, he will oversee the firm's public- and private-sector project management and leverage 30–40 years of relationships to expand the AEC firm's market share.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. However, Badame's appointment signals continued M&A and talent consolidation within AEC firms; developers should expect ongoing shifts in project delivery partnerships and pricing as boutique/mid-market firms compete for marquee talent. Bravo's growth ambitions may increase competition for development management services on large mixed-use and vertical projects.
